To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have shown the possibility of using a combination of Gabor filters and regular trainable weights to reduce energy consumption of CNN training, with a negligible accuracy loss.

the proposed Gabor-based CNNs are 1.31-1.53x more energy-efficient than the baseline CNNs, with 0-3% degradation in accuracy, and that the degradation can be reduced to 1% if the Gabor kernels are partially trained.

we propose a novel CNN implementation, which uses Gabor filters to replace certain weight kernels of the CNN, and show that this approach can achieve significant improvement in training energy and time in exchange for tolerability in accuracy degradation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy-efficient implementation of CNNs, by replacing certain weight filters with Gabor filters, which are pre-trained and fixed, to extract intrinsic features.
the design of an approximate CNN implementation that is energy efficient and has low training complexity, with minimal accuracy degradation.
the energy-efficient implementation of CNNs for computer vision applications.

the proposed approach can be used as an effective energy and time-efficient alternative to the conventional CNN implementation, with a tolerable degradation in the accuracy.

our proposed approach can be used to train large networks with a significant improvement in terms of energy, memory access energy, training time and storage, at the cost of a negligible accuracy loss.
the Gabor filter based CNN implementation is a good compromise between energy and accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can achieve 1.4x faster training time, 1.5x lower energy consumption, and 2.23x lower storage requirement for a given accuracy.
, we have shown that the proposed approach is a promising solution for energy-efficient training of CNNs, with a small accuracy degradation.
the proposed approach yields significant improvement in energy and training time, while suffering a tolerable accuracy degradation, which is acceptable for most real-world applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by replacing some of the trainable weight kernels in CNN with Gabor kernels, we can obtain a significant reduction in training complexity and energy consumption, without a large degradation in classification performance.
, the use of Gabor filters in CNNs, not only helps in reducing training energy, but also helps in reducing the memory access energy and the storage requirements.
, by judiciously replacing certain weight kernels with Gabor filters, one can obtain significant energy and time savings, while suffering tolerable accuracy degradation.
